name: Venkat Rangan
current_role: Co-founder and founding CTO, Clari (now merged with Salesloft; combined company operates under the Salesloft brand)
profile: Indian-born engineer (IIT Madras; MS computer science, University of Miami) who co-founded revenue-forecasting SaaS Clari with Andy Byrne in 2012-13 and served as CTO. Earlier co-founded e-discovery firm Clearwell Systems (acquired by Symantec in 2011). Clari merged with Salesloft in 2025; his current operating title post-merger was not confirmed.
interesting_fact: Before Clari he co-founded and was CTO of e-discovery company Clearwell Systems, which Symantec acquired in 2011.
deep_cut_fact: He first met his Clari co-founder Andy Byrne in the late 1990s at VitalSigns Software, a network-diagnostics startup where Rangan was an engineer and Byrne got his first product management job (1997).
notes: Low public profile; Clari now operates as Salesloft (Steve Cox CEO). Best route likely via LinkedIn or Salesloft/Clari press team. No personal published email found.

name: Ikkjin Ahn
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Moloco
profile: Korean-born ML engineer (BS Seoul National University; MSE UPenn) who worked at Google/YouTube before co-founding Moloco in 2013. Moloco builds machine-learning performance advertising for mobile apps and commerce media and has been reported to be weighing an IPO.
interesting_fact: At Google he developed YouTube's video profitability prediction system; that work on early YouTube monetization revealed the ML-for-mobile-ads opportunity that led to Moloco.
deep_cut_fact: He was the founding Tech Lead Manager of Google's Android Data team before leaving to start Moloco with a small team of ML engineers.
notes: Moloco's PR team publishes a dedicated how-to-contact page; press route is the best bet.

name: Abhinav Shashank
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Innovaccer
profile: IIT Kharagpur graduate who co-founded Innovaccer (with Kanav Hasija and Sandeep Gupta) as a data analytics startup and pivoted it to healthcare around 2016. Innovaccer, based in San Francisco, became India-origin's first healthtech unicorn and now sells an AI/data platform and agents for US health systems.
interesting_fact: Named to Forbes 30 Under 30 Asia 2017 (Enterprise Tech) and has published 300+ articles in international media outlets.
deep_cut_fact: He and co-founder Kanav Hasija were IIT Kharagpur batchmates who graduated in 2010; Abhinav then spent about three years at Ingersoll (Rand) working alongside future co-founder Sandeep Gupta before starting the company.
notes: Active on LinkedIn and frequent media contributor; press team handles interview requests.

name: Wally Ibrahim
current_role: Technical co-founder and CTO, Aloi (integrations platform); co-founder and former CTO of project44
profile: Chicago technologist who co-founded supply-chain visibility platform project44 with Jett McCandless in 2014 and served as its CTO (until about 2018). He has since been CTO and co-founder of Aloi, a platform for building and sharing business integrations. project44 has been valued at about $2.7B.
interesting_fact: Co-founded project44 in Chicago in 2014 with CEO Jett McCandless; project44 grew into one of the leading real-time freight/supply-chain visibility platforms.
notes: Low public profile; sources are mostly third-party profiles (Crunchbase, MarketScreener). No published contact found; LinkedIn likely the only route. Not currently at project44 (CEO is Jett McCandless).

name: Xavier Durand
current_role: Co-founder of Aircall (left the company in late 2020); current role not found
profile: French engineer with front-end development expertise who co-founded cloud phone-system company Aircall in 2014 at the eFounders startup studio in Paris, alongside Olivier Pailhes, Jonathan Anguelov and Pierre-Baptiste Bechu. Aircall became eFounders' first unicorn in 2020; Durand left in late 2020.
interesting_fact: Aircall's founders went through the 500 Startups 2015 batch in San Francisco, then raised $2.75M; within five months the team grew from 5 to 15 and turnover tripled.
deep_cut_fact: When Aircall struggled with hiring and fundraising, Durand moved to New York with CEO Olivier Pailhes while the technical team stayed in Paris -- a split that became a blueprint for French founders building in the US.
notes: Very low public profile and no longer at Aircall; contact@aircall.io is a company address, not his. LinkedIn is likely the only route.

name: Li Hongbo
current_role: Co-founder, executive Director, CTO and Vice President, Geek+ (Geekplus Technology, HKEX-listed)
profile: Beijing robotics engineer (PhD Tsinghua University, 2009) who was a postdoc and associate researcher in Tsinghua's computer science department before co-founding warehouse-robot maker Geek+ with CEO Zheng Yong in February 2015. Geek+ builds autonomous mobile robots for logistics and listed in Hong Kong in 2025; he leads its technology and R&D.
interesting_fact: Before co-founding Geek+ he was a postdoctoral researcher and associate researcher in Tsinghua University's Department of Computer Science and Technology.
deep_cut_fact: Recognised as a professor-level senior engineer by Beijing's senior professional qualification committee (May 2019) and receives a special government allowance from China's State Council (since June 2024); also named an Outstanding Young Member of the China Federation of Logistics & Purchasing.
notes: Chinese-language outreach likely more effective; company IR/PR are the published routes. Li Hongbo is a common name - this is the Geek+ CTO (李洪波).

name: Ruben Drong
current_role: Co-founder, Papaya Global (named Chief Innovation Officer in 2022)
profile: Israeli serial entrepreneur and software engineer who co-founded global payroll and workforce-payments platform Papaya Global in 2016 with Eynat Guez and Ofer Herman. He was Papaya's first Chief Product Officer, charting its technology vision, before moving in 2022 to Chief Innovation Officer focused on long-term strategy.
interesting_fact: As Papaya Global's first Chief Product Officer he set the technology vision for a platform that now runs payroll and payments in 160+ countries; in 2022 he shifted to Chief Innovation Officer.
notes: Low public profile; CEO Eynat Guez is the company's public face. Earlier ventures (AASL, SafelyGuard, MRD-IT) appear only on aggregator profiles, so not used. Best route LinkedIn or Papaya PR.

name: Juan Gonzalez
current_role: Co-founder, Xendit (listed by Y Combinator as Founder/Principal Software Engineer)
profile: Software engineer who co-founded Jakarta-based payments infrastructure company Xendit in 2015 with Moses Lo, Tessa Wijaya and Bo Chen; the company went through Y Combinator (Summer 2015). Xendit started as a consumer fintech app before pivoting to payment APIs for businesses across Southeast Asia, reaching unicorn status in 2021.
interesting_fact: Xendit was part of Y Combinator's Summer 2015 batch and became a unicorn in 2021 after a $150M round led by Tiger Global.
deep_cut_fact: Xendit was originally launched in 2015 as a consumer-focused fintech before the founders pivoted to B2B payment infrastructure.
notes: Very low public profile and common name - verify any LinkedIn match against Xendit. CEO Moses Lo is the public face.

name: Tony He
current_role: Co-founder (and former partner) of Amber Group; current role not confirmed
profile: Hong Kong-based former Morgan Stanley fixed-income trader who co-founded crypto financial-services firm Amber Group (c. 2017) with Michael Wu, Wayne Huo, Tiantian Kullander and Luke Li. Amber reached a $3B valuation in 2022; its Amber Premium business later listed on Nasdaq as Amber International. Crunchbase lists him as a former co-founder and partner.
interesting_fact: Named to Forbes 30 Under 30 (2019) alongside Amber co-founders Tiantian Kullander and Wayne Huo.
deep_cut_fact: All of Amber's co-founders, including He, started out on Morgan Stanley's fixed-income trading floor before leaving to build the company.
notes: Very low public profile (also known as Tony YuHao He; studied at Johns Hopkins per Crunchbase). Common name - verify carefully. Avoid referencing co-founder Kullander's death.

name: Erik Goldman
current_role: Co-founder of Vanta (left the company in 2020); current role not found
profile: Software engineer (reportedly ex-Dropbox, Stanford) who co-founded compliance-automation company Vanta with CEO Christina Cacioppo, working on the initial SOC 2 automation product; Vanta went through Y Combinator and is now valued at about $4B. He left Vanta in 2020.
interesting_fact: Co-founded Vanta, which pioneered automated SOC 2 / security compliance for startups and grew into a multibillion-dollar company.
notes: Very low public profile and a common name (several other Erik Goldmans in tech, e.g. Limelight Labs and Sfara founders) - verify identity before outreach. No published contact found.

name: Alex Zaccaria
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Linktree
profile: Melbourne entrepreneur who co-founded link-in-bio platform Linktree in 2016 with his brother Anthony and Nick Humphreys, after spotting the 'one link' problem while running music/digital agency Bolster. Linktree now serves tens of millions of creators and businesses; he is pushing the company into AI and commerce and is also an angel investor.
interesting_fact: Linktree began as an internal fix at Bolster, the digital agency the Zaccaria brothers ran for musicians and festivals, where managing clients' social accounts exposed the single-bio-link limit.
deep_cut_fact: Before Linktree he ran club nights and side businesses, including selling music consumables like guitar strings and drumsticks, and 'Happy Hobo', a mattress that turns a car's back seat into a bed or couch.
notes: Accessible, media-friendly CEO (podcasts, conference speaker e.g. HumanX). Press email is the best route.

name: Ryan Noon
current_role: Co-founder and Chairman, Material Security (CEO until 2023)
profile: Stanford-trained security engineer (BS CS; MS computer networks and security) who co-founded Material Security in 2017 with Abhishek Agrawal and led it as CEO before becoming Chairman in 2023. Material secures Microsoft 365 and Google Workspace email and files; Noon previously led engineering teams at Dropbox and Ayasdi.
interesting_fact: Material Security protects cloud email and productivity suites (Microsoft 365, Google Workspace) and reached unicorn status; Noon handed the CEO role to co-founder Abhishek Agrawal in 2023 and became Chairman.
deep_cut_fact: His previous startup, Parastructure, was acquired by Dropbox (2014), where he went on to lead engineering teams.
notes: Has appeared on security podcasts and written for SC World. No published email found; LinkedIn or Material's site likely best.

name: Michael Cassau
current_role: Founder and CEO, SKROL (Miami); founder and former CEO of Grover
profile: German entrepreneur, ex-Goldman Sachs investment professional and Rocket Internet executive, who founded Berlin tech-rental/subscription platform Grover in 2015 and grew it into a unicorn that raised about $2B. He stepped back from Grover at the end of 2023 and in 2024 launched SKROL in Miami, an AI-driven platform to acquire and grow small and medium-sized businesses.
interesting_fact: Grover pioneered renting rather than buying consumer electronics (phones, laptops, consoles) on monthly subscriptions and entered the US market via Miami.
deep_cut_fact: For SKROL he brought former Grover CTO Christopher Silva and finance lead Mitja Sadar with him; SKROL targets mainly brick-and-mortar SMBs and explicitly avoids restaurants, Amazon FBA and Shopify stores.
notes: Now Miami-based; no longer runs Grover (CEO Rob Straathof). No published personal contact found; LinkedIn or SKROL likely best.

name: Samuel Mueller
current_role: CEO and Co-founder, Scandit
profile: Swiss computer scientist (PhD ETH Zurich; MSc CS and MA financial economics, University of Zurich) who co-founded Zurich-based Scandit in 2009 with Christian Floerkemeier and Christof Roduner. Scandit sells smartphone-based barcode, ID and label scanning plus store-intelligence software powered by computer vision and AI to retailers, logistics and airlines.
interesting_fact: Scandit started from the idea of bridging physical objects and digital information, using barcodes as the entry point just as phone cameras were becoming ubiquitous.
deep_cut_fact: Before Scandit he was a corporate researcher at IBM Zurich Research Lab, earning three IBM Invention Achievement Awards and an IBM Research Division Award; his ETH PhD was in computer science and temporal logics.
notes: Regular conference speaker and podcast guest; press email is the best route.

name: Hayden Adams
current_role: Founder and CEO, Uniswap Labs
profile: Former Siemens mechanical engineer (Stony Brook grad) who taught himself Solidity in 2017 and launched Uniswap, the automated-market-maker decentralized exchange on Ethereum, in November 2018. As CEO of Uniswap Labs he leads development of the Uniswap protocol, wallet and the Unichain layer-2 network.
interesting_fact: Uniswap was inspired by a Vitalik Buterin blog post on automated market makers; it launched on Ethereum mainnet on November 2, 2018 and became the largest decentralized exchange.
deep_cut_fact: Karl Floersch showcased Adams' early Uniswap demo in a Devcon 3 talk; an attendee, Pascal Van Hecke, then reached out and gave him a grant to fund his next month of research, kick-starting weekly calls that kept the project going.
notes: Very active on X (@haydenzadams); that is the most direct public route. Media inquiries via media@uniswap.org.

name: Jack Groetzinger
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, SeatGeek
profile: Cleveland-raised Dartmouth economics graduate and former Bain associate consultant who co-founded ticket search-and-sell platform SeatGeek in 2009 with college friend Russ D'Souza. SeatGeek grew from a ticket search engine into a primary ticketing provider for major sports teams and venues; he has also been a partner at seed fund Founder Collective.
interesting_fact: The idea for SeatGeek came from Groetzinger and D'Souza buying and reselling sports tickets for extra money and noticing how opaque secondary-ticket pricing was.
deep_cut_fact: Before SeatGeek, he and Russ D'Souza co-founded Scribnia, a web app that used collaborative filtering to recommend bloggers.
notes: press@seatgeek.com appears as the press contact on SeatGeek releases (2022, 2025). Former startup-event speaker; reasonably accessible via PR.

name: Jim Jacobsen
current_role: Co-founder of Cart.com (listed as Executive Chairman in company/market profiles); founder of Bearing Ventures
profile: Houston entrepreneur and investor who co-founded e-commerce services company Cart.com with CEO Omair Tariq in October 2020. He previously helped scale consumer brands including RTIC Outdoors (coolers/drinkware) and founded Houston venture firm Bearing Ventures in 2017.
interesting_fact: At RTIC Outdoors and other ventures he scaled brands to $200-300M in sales, building the full e-commerce chain 'from the factory floor to the customer's door' - the playbook Cart.com was built to sell.
notes: Low media profile; Omair Tariq is Cart.com's public face. Current Cart.com title uncertain (not shown in leadership grid). No published contact found.

name: Tamar Bar-Ilan
current_role: Co-founder and CTO, Cyera
profile: Israeli engineer (BSc physics and computer science, Hebrew University) and Talpiot graduate who co-founded AI-native data security company Cyera in 2021 with CEO Yotam Segev. Cyera, based in New York and Tel Aviv, discovers and classifies sensitive data across clouds and has become one of the fastest-growing cybersecurity unicorns; she leads product and engineering.
interesting_fact: She and Yotam Segev met in the IDF's elite Talpiot program and together founded, built and ran the cloud security division of Unit 8200.
deep_cut_fact: After leaving the army in early 2020 she and Segev spent most of that year as 'independent entrepreneurs in our living rooms, learning how to set up a company' - Cyera is her first job after military service.
notes: Rare example of a female cybersecurity unicorn co-founder/CTO; press route via press@cyera.io.

name: Ben Thompson
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Employment Hero
profile: Sydney-based former employment lawyer who co-founded HR, payroll and hiring platform Employment Hero in 2014 with CTO Dave Tong, after seeing small-business clients of his father's firm Employment Innovations struggle with employment admin. Employment Hero is now a multi-billion-dollar SME 'employment OS' operating in Australia, NZ, the UK, Singapore, Malaysia and Canada.
interesting_fact: Named Technology category winner at the EY Entrepreneur Of The Year Australia 2026 awards.
deep_cut_fact: In Employment Hero's early years he ran four companies at once (including Employment Innovations and Power2Motivate) from one floor above Sydney's Wynyard Station, and he has run a strict 90-day execution cadence borrowed from Verne Harnish's 'Rockefeller Habits' since around 2005.
notes: Media-friendly founder (podcasts, Founder Friday). Not to be confused with Stratechery's Ben Thompson.

name: Yang Yu
current_role: Founder of Chengdu Coco Cartoon (可可豆动画); animation director known as Jiaozi (饺子)
profile: Yang Yu (b. 1980, Luzhou, Sichuan), known professionally as Jiaozi, is a pharmacy graduate of Sichuan University turned self-taught animator who co-founded the studio that became Chengdu Coco Cartoon in 2009. He wrote and directed Ne Zha (2019) and Ne Zha 2 (2025); the sequel became the highest-grossing animated film worldwide and China's top-grossing film ever.
interesting_fact: Ne Zha 2 made him the first non-Hollywood director with a US$1B and then US$2B film, and the first animation director to earn US$2B; with just two features he became China's highest-grossing director.
deep_cut_fact: His December 2008 debut short 'See Through' (打，打个大西瓜) won the Special Jury Prize in the international competition of the 26th Berlin International Short Film Festival and Gold at Japan's TBS DigiCon6 - a decade before Ne Zha made him famous.
notes: Hurun listing 'Coco Cartoon' = Chengdu Coco Cartoon (可可豆动画), originally the 饺克力 studio he co-founded with Liu Wenzhang in 2009 (per moegirl wiki). Very private; outreach would need to go via the studio or distributor Enlight Media, in Chinese.
